title: The Beloved Judy Blume
summary: Josh and Chuck (the iHeart Intro speaker is labeled as Chuck in the banter) celebrate Judy Blume, covering her Elizabeth, New Jersey childhood, family losses and anxiety, marriage and early motherhood, her start as a children's author with The One in the Middle Is the Green Kangaroo and Iggy's House, the breakthrough Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret, the adult novels, the frequent book bans of Forever and others, her anti-censorship activism, her 2023 JK Rowling comments controversy, her Key West life and the 2026 Oppenheimer biography rift. The episode ends with a listener mail about a Massey Hall Toronto show.
topics: Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret

entities.name: Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret

segments.title: Opening banter on Judy Blume books
segments.summary: The hosts compare which Judy Blume books they read as kids, including Tales of a Fourth Grade Nothing, Superfudge and Are You There God, and mention Ramona Quimby books.

segments.title: Judy Blume's childhood in Elizabeth, New Jersey
segments.summary: Blume was born Judith Marcia Sussman in 1938 in Elizabeth, New Jersey, to a dentist father and homemaker mother. She was an anxious child who loved reading and imaginary play, and her father was her confidant.

segments.title: Hosts' kids and reading
segments.summary: The hosts discuss their own children's reading habits and imaginative play, with Chuck describing his daughter's notebook at a basketball game.

segments.title: Blume's piano lessons and imaginary students
segments.summary: While practicing piano, Blume taught imaginary students and tracked their progress in a notebook. She did not initially aspire to be a writer.

segments.title: Anxiety, family loss and the Newark plane crashes
segments.summary: Blume was anxious as a child, worried about her father's health after uncles died of heart problems, and had obsessive compulsive behaviors when her family moved to Miami Beach for her brother's illness. Three Newark Airport plane crashes in fifty-eight days, which killed about a hundred people including eleven residents of Elizabeth, affected her childhood.

segments.title: College years at NYU
segments.summary: Blume graduated high school at the top of her class and attended NYU, where she was drawn to bohemian and beatnik culture.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Mid-episode ad break.

segments.title: Marriage, early career path and women writers
segments.summary: Blume married lawyer John Bloom in 1959 after her father died a month before the wedding. She graduated in 1961 with an early childhood education degree and had two children. The hosts discuss how S.E. Hinton used initials because publishing was closed to young women.

segments.title: Path to publication and Iggy's House
segments.summary: Blume began writing picture books for her kids after years of rejection. A late-1960s NYU continuing education writing class was a turning point. Her first published book was The One in the Middle Is the Green Kangaroo and her first novel was Iggy's House (1970), about white flight and racial tensions seen through a white girl's eyes.
topics: The One in the Middle Is the Green Kangaroo

segments.title: Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret and its impact
segments.summary: Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret was published in 1970 and became a New York Times bestseller. The hosts describe it as a trailblazing book about preadolescence, with the Preteen Sensations club and the bust-increasing passage. The 1970s-era movie is mentioned, and the trade paperback in 1972 made it affordable.
topics: Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret

segments.title: Blume's divorce and productivity in the 1970s
segments.summary: Blume divorced John Bloom in 1975 and married physicist Thomas Kitchens, living in London and New Mexico. She published about ten books between 1970 and 1975.

segments.title: Forever and the book-banning target
segments.summary: Forever (1975) follows a teen girl having sex for the first time, and the hosts describe it as a safe-sex guide. Its frank content made Blume a target for book challenges, and her books are often on banned lists.

segments.title: Why conservatives challenge Blume's books
segments.summary: The hosts discuss why Blume's books draw challenges, linking them to second wave feminism and conservative views about teaching kids about sexuality. Josh says he opposes banning books while understanding parents' concerns.

segments.title: Tiger Eyes and bans
segments.summary: Tiger Eyes deals with a girl whose father is killed in a convenience store robbery, grief, depression, and underage drinking, and is also often banned.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Brief break before the next segment.

segments.title: Adult novels, critics and reading nostalgia
segments.summary: Blume wrote four adult novels, including Wifey (1978), Smart Women (1983), Summer Sisters (1998) and In the Unlikely Event (2015). Critics sometimes called her simplistic. The hosts discuss childhood series like Sweet Valley High, Nancy Drew and Hardy Boys.

segments.title: Anti-censorship activism and parent-child communication
segments.summary: Blume became a central figure in the anti-book-banning movement, working with the National Coalition Against Censorship and running projects in the 1980s, including Kids Fun Capitol and Letters to Judy (1986), a book of children's letters.

segments.title: JK Rowling comments and Blume's clarification
segments.summary: In 2023 an interview with The Times of London quoted Blume supporting JK Rowling. Blume said she was taken out of context and affirmed support for the trans community. Ninety million copies sold in forty languages.

segments.title: Documentary, biographies and personal life
segments.summary: A 2023 documentary Bloom Forever and a 2024 biography The Genius of Judy were released. Mark Oppenheimer's 2026 book Judy Blume Forever: A Life drew a rift after Blume cut off contact with him. Blume met George Cooper in 1979 and married him in 1987; they run a bookstore in Key West.

segments.title: Closing thoughts on Blume
segments.summary: The hosts praise Blume's bravery and encourage listeners to read her books at libraries or independent bookstores.

segments.title: Listener mail from Kelsey and Andrew
segments.summary: Kelsey and Andrew write about attending the hosts' live show at Massey Hall in Toronto in June and thank them for the evening.
